title: Sports Complex Deal Development
subtitle: Deal structuring, investor materials, and capital campaign planning for a 34-acre youth sports development.
summary: This first public version shows the narrative, financial sandbox, and styled highlight asset while keeping the proposal PDF and workbook archived as restricted records.

kpiSummary.budget: $16.29M total capital requirement spanning construction, renovation, reserves, and fee structure.
kpiSummary.rates: Milestone-based consulting scope designed as a full deal-development engagement rather than hourly advisory.
kpiSummary.outcomes: Proves the ability to design a multi-stream business model, investor stack, and phased operating plan for a non-standard real estate asset.
challenges: Construction had started before the business model and fundraising engine were fully in place.
The story had to bridge youth sports, real estate, hospitality, and operations into one investable narrative.
The engagement stretched beyond documents into phased PM and campaign sequencing.

carousel.title: 1. The Situation
carousel.heading: Construction had started. Money had not been secured.
carousel.content: A youth sports academy in Conyers, Georgia had already broken ground on a 34-acre property — but without a business model, investor materials, or a capital campaign to fund completion. Construction had started. Money had not been secured.

carousel.title: 2. The Approach
carousel.heading: Five sequential phases
carousel.content: The engagement was structured across five sequential phases, each with defined milestones, deliverable deadlines, and fee invoices tied directly to delivery — not to time.

carousel.title: 3. The Financial Model
carousel.heading: Seven distinct income streams
carousel.content: The revenue model identified seven distinct income streams across the 34-acre complex. All figures are gross revenue projections from the financial model.

carousel.title: 4. The Deliverable Stack
carousel.heading: 18 distinct deliverable categories
carousel.content: The engagement produced 18 distinct deliverable categories across five phases spanning business and financial materials, investor relations, and brand and operations systems.

carousel.title: 5. The Fee Structure
carousel.heading: $352,205 fixed-fee engagement
carousel.content: Total engagement fee: $352,205 — structured as fixed-fee milestones tied to deliverables, not hourly billing. Equivalent market-rate services from large management consulting firms were benchmarked at $1,126,475 for the same scope.

carousel.title: 6. What This Demonstrates
carousel.heading: End-to-end deal development
carousel.content: The consultant was not engaged to do one thing. The scope ran from raw vision articulation through business model design, financial modeling, entity structuring, investor materials production, capital campaign management, and post-funding operations oversight.

carousel.title: 7. Portfolio Card
carousel.heading: Management Consulting Proposal + Financial Model
carousel.content: This engagement proves the consultant can hold the entire arc of a complex development deal — from structuring the business model and building investor-grade financials, to designing and running the capital campaign, to managing phased operations after funding.
